# Deep Research Intelligence Packet

## Cycle metadata

- Packet ID: `dr-20260921-1906-candidate-validation`
- Research system: `Codex web research`
- Started at: `2026-09-21 19:06 CDT`
- Completed at: `2026-09-21 19:08 CDT`
- Research scope: Four unresolved candidate-page validations for Jack in the Box, Papa Johns, and Cracker Barrel
- Queue item or vendor: Restaurant365, PAR Technology, and Crunchtime candidate pages
- Methodology: Candidate-page validation using the direct vendor-published pages; deployment scope and historical limitations retained explicitly

## Executive result

- Pages reviewed: 4
- Candidate pages validated: 4
- Brand-vendor-product observations added or revised: 3
- Conflicts found: 1
- Material takeaway: The Jack in the Box and Papa Johns pages support unusually strong systemwide selections, but Papa Johns is a planned transition through the end of 2027 rather than a completed installed base. The two Cracker Barrel pages support one historical 2016 back-office relationship and are not independent corroboration.

## Evidence observations

### Observation 1

- Brand: Jack in the Box
- Vendor: Restaurant365
- Product or category: Mandated back-office inventory platform; accounting, financial reporting, AP automation, and multi-entity management at a subset of restaurants
- Relationship indication: `customer`
- Deployment scope: `enterprise`
- Evidence type: `press release`
- Confidence: `95%`
- Confidence rationale: Restaurant365 reports a completed rollout across all corporate and franchise locations and quotes the Jack in the Box CTO. This is strong first-party/vendor evidence, though not independent third-party verification.
- Source title: Jack in the Box Selects Restaurant365 as its Sole Back-Office Inventory Platform
- Source URL: https://www.restaurant365.com/in-the-news/jack-in-the-box-selects-restaurant365-as-its-sole-back-office-inventory-platform/
- Publisher or source owner: Restaurant365
- Published date, if known: 2026-03-05
- Accessed date: `2026-09-21`
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: Restaurant365 says its inventory platform was mandated and deployed across all 2,128 Jack in the Box corporate and franchise locations after a proof of concept and pilot. It separately says Restaurant365 provides the accounting engine for approximately half of the restaurants.
- Product-specific evidence: Centralized inventory across 2,128 locations; approximately half also use accounting, real-time financial reporting, AP automation, and multi-entity management.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: Vendor-published announcement; the accounting footprint is only approximately half of locations and must not be generalized to the full system.
- Recommended follow-up: Seek an independent Jack in the Box filing, franchise communication, or implementation update confirming current rollout status and location count.

### Observation 2

- Brand: Papa Johns
- Vendor: PAR Technology
- Product or category: PAR POS and PAR OPS for front-of-house ordering, make-line operations, above-restaurant management, labor, inventory, and restaurant management
- Relationship indication: `customer`
- Deployment scope: `enterprise`
- Evidence type: `press release`
- Confidence: `95%`
- Confidence rationale: PAR reports a named enterprise selection with an on-record Papa Johns technology executive quote and a defined U.S. rollout plan. Confidence applies to the selection, not to completion of deployment.
- Source title: Papa Johns Partners with PAR Technology to Power POS and OPS Transformation Across 3,200 U.S. Restaurants
- Source URL: https://partech.com/news-coverage/papa-johns-partners-with-par-technology-to-power-pos-and-ops-transformation-across-3200-u-s-restaurants/
- Publisher or source owner: PAR Technology
- Published date, if known: 2026-01-12
- Accessed date: `2026-09-21`
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: Papa Johns selected PAR POS and PAR OPS for its next-generation U.S. restaurant stack. The stated plan is to transition corporate and franchise locations from legacy on-premise systems, with full system rollout planned by the end of 2027.
- Product-specific evidence: PAR POS and PAR OPS; ordering, make-line operations, above-store management, AI-supported labor, inventory, restaurant management, shared data, and unified support.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: This is a rollout commitment, not evidence that all 3,200 U.S. restaurants are already live. Do not convert the headline's scope into a current installed-base claim.
- Recommended follow-up: Track implementation milestones and look for Papa Johns reporting that distinguishes selected, in rollout, and live locations.

### Observation 3

- Brand: Cracker Barrel
- Vendor: Crunchtime
- Product or category: Back-of-house restaurant management, labor cost management, inventory cost management, and operational efficiency
- Relationship indication: `customer`
- Deployment scope: `historical`
- Evidence type: `press release`
- Confidence: `80%`
- Confidence rationale: Two Crunchtime pages explicitly describe the 2016 selection across the organization, but both are same-publisher pages dated the same day and do not independently confirm that the relationship remains active in 2026.
- Source title: Cracker Barrel Old Country Store Selects Crunchtime; Cracker Barrel Uses Crunchtime to Optimize BOH
- Source URL: https://www.crunchtime.com/press/cracker-barrel-old-country-store-selects-crunchtime ; https://www.crunchtime.com/press/cracker-barrel-selects-crunchtime
- Publisher or source owner: Crunchtime
- Published date, if known: 2016-06-01
- Accessed date: `2026-09-21`
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: Crunchtime says Cracker Barrel selected its restaurant-management software in 2016 to improve operational efficiency and reduce labor and inventory costs across the organization.
- Product-specific evidence: Back-of-house restaurant management, labor cost reduction, inventory cost reduction, operational visibility, and agility.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The selection page says more than 640 locations in 43 states and its company boilerplate says 641; the companion page says more than 680 locations in 45 states while later boilerplate says more than 660. These pages are duplicate first-party evidence and support only a historical 2016 relationship, not a current 2026 footprint.
- Recommended follow-up: Find a dated Cracker Barrel source or current Crunchtime customer story confirming whether the platform is still deployed and at what scope.

## Negative findings

- Candidate or claim: The two Cracker Barrel URLs might represent independent corroboration or current deployment evidence.
- Pages checked: Both Crunchtime URLs in the source ledger.
- Result: They are same-publisher pages dated the same day describing the same 2016 selection. They are useful historical evidence but not independent corroboration and not proof of a current 2026 installed base.

## Source ledger

| URL | Source type | Accessed | Supports observation(s) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| https://www.restaurant365.com/in-the-news/jack-in-the-box-selects-restaurant365-as-its-sole-back-office-inventory-platform/ | Press release / vendor news | 2026-09-21 | Observation 1 | Strong systemwide inventory rollout; accounting only at approximately half of restaurants. |
| https://partech.com/news-coverage/papa-johns-partners-with-par-technology-to-power-pos-and-ops-transformation-across-3200-u-s-restaurants/ | Press release / vendor news | 2026-09-21 | Observation 2 | Strong selection evidence; rollout is planned through end of 2027, not complete. |
| https://www.crunchtime.com/press/cracker-barrel-old-country-store-selects-crunchtime | Press release | 2026-09-21 | Observation 3 | Historical 2016 selection; same-publisher duplicate evidence. |
| https://www.crunchtime.com/press/cracker-barrel-selects-crunchtime | Vendor customer story | 2026-09-21 | Observation 3 | Historical 2016 BOH detail; location counts conflict with companion page. |

## Research notes and inferences

- Inference: Jack in the Box has stronger current deployment evidence than most candidate pages because the source describes a completed systemwide rollout and separately scopes the partial accounting footprint.
- Inference: Papa Johns should be represented as selected/in rollout until a later source confirms live deployment progress; the 3,200 figure is intended rollout scope.
- Inference: Cracker Barrel's relationship is durable historical evidence but should not be refreshed into a current canonical claim without a more recent source.
